question: According to the Andersen Behavioural Model of health service utilisation, which three categories of factors determine whether an individual seeks formal healthcare?

answers.text: Predisposing factors, enabling factors, and need factors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The Andersen model organises determinants of health-seeking into predisposing (demographics, beliefs), enabling (income, insurance, proximity), and need (perceived or evaluated illness severity) factors.

answers.text: Individual factors, community factors, and system factors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. This is a general social-ecological framing, not the specific Andersen model taxonomy. The Andersen model uses predisposing, enabling, and need as its three domains.

answers.text: Biological factors, psychological factors, and social factors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The biopsychosocial framework is a different model. The Andersen Behavioural Model specifically uses predisposing, enabling, and need factors to explain health-service utilisation patterns.

answers.text: Supply factors, demand factors, and barrier factors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Supply-demand framing is used in health economics. The Andersen model focuses on the patient side: predisposing characteristics, enabling resources, and perceived/evaluated need.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Andersen Behavioural Model uses three categories: (1) Predisposing factors — age, sex, health beliefs; (2) Enabling factors — income, insurance, distance to facility; (3) Need factors — perceived illness severity or clinician-evaluated need. Review block 5 to map Indian examples to each category.
Excellent. Predisposing, enabling, and need — this triad is the foundation of the Andersen model and frequently appears in community medicine examinations.
